title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Faulkner will not let them get set. White mixes the odd front and moves Woods. That is the tape.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — condensed session with Charles. Fan rail stays empty.
headline: The fans do not need a box score. They need to see why FAU could not get set on offense and why the short throw kept living on defense. Faulkner’s night is the looks. White’s night is the 3-3-5 and Woods.

What the fans want on Faulkner is the complexity of the looks.

He will not let them get set. That is the hire. Two tight ends and a read. Same family, the line washes one way and Baugh takes the other hole. Then Brown is in motion four yards deep, the pullers sell counter, the interior is out in front of the screen, and the ball goes to the motion man. Then it is pistol, an H-back, and three wide — a run that does not look like a run. Then motion one way, tackles the other, Philo pulls it when the end crashes. Then the same pistol set, play-action, Wilson sitting under the zone, and they are out of second-and-12. Then the short throw to Brown with the corner off — first miss, he is gone. Then Brown is the runner. Then Abrams over the top when they crowd the run. Then Clark when Baugh is off — he runs, and he scores when they stay in on the give. Then the 61 when everybody in the building knows it is a run.

That is the complexity. Not a new trick every snap. The defense has to check the back, the H, the motion, and the wide people when they break. They do not know if it is the give, the keep, the screen, or the throw off the run. FootballScoop’s coordinator of the year at Georgia Tech did not win with one picture. He won by dressing the same ideas up until you step wrong.

What looked good: Baugh on the read when they knew it was coming. The wash-and-cut. The counter-to-screen to Brown. Wilson on the sit. The 49 to Brown. Abrams when they finally sat on the run. The sneak on fourth-and-1. Harpring in the middle. The 61. Clark as the runner and as the receiver. They still take the points from 53 when the drive stalls.

What to clean: the keep when Sledge crashes and is still there. The snap that loses twenty inside the five. The ball that comes off Mays. Those are real. They are not the night. The night is FAU never knowing what is coming out of the huddle.
bullets: The looks keep changing. The play stays simple for Baugh, Brown, Wilson, Philo.

What looked good: the run when they knew, the screen off the pullers, Wilson getting them out of second-and-12, the 49, the 61.
Clean the snap and the keep Sledge won. That is the list.

What the fans want on White is the 3-3-5 and what he does with Woods.

He will play a 3-3-5. Three down. JACK as a stand-up. Two linebackers. Five DBs. Then he will space the tackles and stand both edges up and run a stunt. Then he will shade three down linemen to one side of the ball and put Woods and a linebacker in the other gap. He does not live in one picture. He changes the look often enough that the line cannot get a clean count. Never every snap — the condensed cut is not the whole series — but often.

Woods is the lever. On third down White moves him. Sometimes he is the end. Sometimes he is a linebacker. If Woods is on the ball, he is the edge. If he is off, the edge belongs to somebody else and Woods is coming or dropping from a different spot. That is how you put your third-down rusher in a better lane without telling the tackle who has him. You saw it on third-and-7 and again on third-and-1. Same rule. Different coverage behind it. Later he is in the run fit — Ervin, Farrow — when they try to stay on schedule.

The coverage mixes too. First money down: press, man, comeback, they convert. Next money down: corners off, nickel on the line, short throw, they convert. Early down: one-high, corners off, Chiles fills the short middle, three yards, they win the snap. Then a wide stunt, still off, still one-high, Valsin converts. Then third-and-10: shade front, press one side, six yards off the other, Coleman sells the middle and takes the outside. That is the plan paying off. Not a blitz they needed. He moved the quarterback’s eyes.

What looked good: Coleman’s bait. Johnson’s pick the same way — he holds it, they take it. The three fourth-down kills, including Bett on the keep at the 1. James and Lyons in the backfield. Chiles on the short middle when the look is one-high. Woods showing up later in the run game when he is asked to tackle. McCloud taking the fourth-and-2 away. James stopping Ervin to end the half.

What leaked: the short stuff. They play off a lot. Henry and Valsin will take the five and the seven and stay on the field. That is ninety snaps. The pile at the 1. The end who leaves and Veltkamp walks in. The fade when the corner is off. Hoch on fourth down. White’s call is the 3-3-5 and Woods. The improvement is get off the field when they throw the hitch, and keep the edge when the quarterback keeps it.
